issue.title: feat(mcp): size cluster screenshots to the clusters, up to 2560px
issue.body:
In order to give agents a picture they can actually read, this PR makes `get_cluster_screenshot` return an image with exactly the aspect ratio of the requested clusters, drawn edge to edge with no margin, at up to 2560px on the longer side. Until now every cluster screenshot was a fixed 1200x630 with a margin. A tall or wide cluster came back small inside empty space, and a cluster wider than about 24,000 page units was cropped, because the camera can't zoom out past 5%. Current vision models read images at full resolution up to a 2576px long edge, so 1200px left most of that unused.

```
get_cluster_screenshot(boardId, page, clusterIds, theme?, size?)
  → page name + PNG at the clusters' aspect ratio, longer side `size` (64–2560, default 2560)
```

A cluster box of 4000x1000 comes back 2560x640, or 800x200 with `size: 800`. Small clusters come back smaller than `size`, because the board is never enlarged more than 8x (the editor's maximum zoom); an 80x40 sticky note is 640x320.

### How it works

- The worker sizes the image from the box around the requested clusters, which the cluster index already stores, so sizing costs no extra measure. With no measured box it falls back to the 1200:630 ratio.
- It signs a new `fit: 'tight'` and that size into the render job. The render page is shared with OG images, which must keep their margin and 200–1600px limits, so the flag is how the page tells the two apart.
- For a tight job the render page exports the shapes' own bounds at the exact scale with `editor.toImage`, instead of fitting the camera. That is what removes the zoom limit, so huge clusters are scaled down rather than cropped. If the bounds have moved since they were measured, they're centred rather than stretched.
- PNG cache keys now carry the size and a `tight-shapes-` prefix, so every cluster screenshot misses the cache once after deploy.

### Decisions worth checking

- **Strokes at the frame edge are clipped.** "No margin" uses geometry bounds, which leave out half the stroke width and arrowhead overhang. A shape touching the edge loses the outer half of its stroke: up to about 14px at the 8x cap on an `m` stroke, which hits handwriting hardest. A perfectly straight horizontal line comes back 1px tall. A small stroke-sized allowance would fix both but adds a few pixels of margin. Open question.
- **The deploy that ships this.** Workers deploy before the client, so for a few minutes the old render page answers tight jobs with its margin and 200–1600px limits, and those images are cached until each board next changes. There's deliberately no guard for it: it only happens once, on this deploy.
- **Live capture trial.** With `THUMBNAIL_RENDER_LIVE_CAPTURE` on, clusters too large for the camera's minimum zoom take the export path instead.
- **Overlap with open PRs.** #11227 changes this tool and the cluster index format, and #11326 and #11345 move MCP screenshots into the user's open tab, which has its own copy of the old margin and zoom clamp (`getExportFrame` in `tabRender.ts`). On top of #11345 most of this PR's render page, token and cache changes would be unnecessary; the sizing and `size` argument would carry over, and the tab's export frame would need the same edge-to-edge change.
- The local evals harness (`evalsLocalMcp.ts`) parses `size` but its fixture screenshots aren't keyed on it.

### Change type

- [x] `feature`

### Test plan

1. On a preview, call `get_page_info` on a board, then `get_cluster_screenshot` for one cluster. The image should match the cluster's aspect ratio, longest side 2560px, with no margin.
2. Repeat with `size: 800`, and with a single small shape (should come back at most 8x its size).
3. Screenshot a cluster that spans more than 30,000 units. It should be whole, not cropped.
4. Load a board's OG image and check it's still 1200x630 with a margin.

- [x] Unit tests
- [ ] End to end tests

No real Browser Run render has been checked yet.

### Release notes

- Return tldraw.com MCP cluster screenshots at the clusters' own aspect ratio, without a margin, at up to 2560px, and add a `size` argument to request a smaller image

### Code changes

| Section   | LOC change |
| --------- | ---------- |
| Core code | +13 / -0   |
| Tests     | +256 / -3  |
| Apps      | +221 / -45 |

issue.title: feat(mcp): edit boards through the user's open tab

labels.name: repo-3bfec0a7
labels.description: New feature

labels.name: repo-3bfec0a7
labels.description: Related to tldraw.com

labels.name: repo-3bfec0a7
labels.description: ⚙️ Deploys a preview of tldraw.com for this PR

issue.body:
In order to let an agent connected to the tldraw.com MCP server edit a board while the user watches, this PR adds an `apply_ops` tool that runs Steve's canvas ops (#11338) in the user's open tab, over the channel from #11326. It's stacked on #11326, and it implements the to-do list in `canvas_todo.md`.

The MCP tools now work only through that tab. Browser Run is gone from them, along with the PNG cache and cluster index only it wrote to, so anything that needs an editor answers with the board's URL when no tab has it open. `get_board_info` and the other tools that need no editor work as before. Thumbnails and OG images still use Browser Run.

Two new tools read what people are doing: `get_board_users`, and `get_user_state` for selection, page and viewport. The per-account rate limit is gone with Browser Run, which is all it bounded, and there's no flag: anyone with MCP access can use `apply_ops`. `search_boards`, `create_board` and `rename_board` keep their limits. "Working in an open tab" in `browser-run-thumbnails.md` has the design.

### Decisions worth checking

- **A write runs exactly once.** The channel's first-answer-wins would apply a batch in every tab. A write goes to the one tab the user was last active in, and that tab applies it only after its `accepted` POST gets a 200. That also stands down a frozen tab that wakes after the job ended.
- **A timeout on a write says what it knows.** Nothing acknowledged means nothing was applied. A timeout after a claim, or the object failing partway, means the batch may have landed, so the agent is told to check before resending. A batch is declined mid-drag, because cancelling a drag rolls back past it, and dropped if it queued for over 5s.
- **Presence is untrusted.** Any client can set any field, read-only guests included, and it reaches an agent that can edit. Identity comes from the verified session, and names and ids are cut down before they reach the model.
- **Reads are live.** This departs from `canvas_todo.md`, which proposes persisting when a batch completes. Page tools read from the durable object rather than R2, so an agent reads what it just drew and nothing needs persisting. Only the requested page crosses the RPC. `get_board_info` needs no tab and still reads R2, so it can lag.
- **`get_user_state` for the caller asks their tab.** This also departs from the spec, which says presence. A hibernating room clears `selectedShapeIds` from presence to fit its socket attachments, so "change what I selected" would read as nothing after a pause. Other users' state does come from presence, and can read as empty for the same reason.
- **A batch for a page the user isn't on is refused.** Ops place shapes on the page in view. This answers an open question in the spec, for now.
- **Write access is checked in the durable object, before it looks for a tab,** with the rule `onRequest` uses, so a view-only caller is told that rather than sent to open the board.
- **The op schema is copied into `dotcom-shared`,** because the worker can't import it without bundling zod. `toolSchema.test.ts` fails if the two drift.
- **Published boards can't be read for now,** apart from `get_board_info`, because the room behind one holds the live file rather than the published copy. Screenshots of a page the user isn't on are refused too. Reverting the fallback removal is what would bring these back.

### Fixed along the way

- **Edits from a hidden tab never reached the server.** The store tells the sync client about changes on an animation frame, and the sync client sends them on one, and neither fires there. The tab looked right, another client saw nothing, and a reload lost it. A user can't edit a hidden tab, so nothing had exercised this. The tab now flushes the store after a batch, and the sync client's scheduler has a timer. Testing this from a second client is misleading, because that client's traffic flushes the edits. See "API changes".
- **`settle()` hung in a hidden tab**, for the same reason, so a batch would apply and never report back.
- **`apply_ops` threw an `EvalError` after a reload.** Zod compiles validators with `new Function`, which tldraw.com's CSP forbids, so canvas ops now set `jitless`.

### Reviewing this

The diff includes #11338 and the 8 `main` commits that branch was on, which accounts for the changes outside `apps/dotcom`, `packages/dotcom-shared`, `packages/sync-core` and `packages/utils`. `packages/dotcom-shared/src/canvasOpsJsonSchema.ts` is a generated copy.

The last commit removes the render page's measure and live capture modes on its own, so it's easy to drop: #11281 builds on `measure`, and this will conflict with it. The cluster index table stays in existing durable objects with nothing reading it, and the `mcp/` R2 bucket's objects expire on their lifecycle rule. `shapeIds` and the `mcp` render token surface are left in the render pipeline with no callers, because removing them means reworking OG's token records and slicing.

### Change type

- [x] `feature`

### Test plan

None of the latest commits have been run: `pnpm typecheck` and lint pass, but no browser checks have run since presence, live reads, the write check and the store flush went in, and the unit tests are new or rewritten. Before those changes, a local browser run against a real durable object covered a batch on a new board, one undo step, two tabs, a hidden tab with a second client present, a frozen tab and no tab.

To test on this preview:

1. Open a board and connect an MCP client to the preview.
2. Call `apply_ops`, then undo. One undo should take the whole batch.
3. Call `get_page_info` straight after `apply_ops`. It should list the new shapes.
4. Select a shape, wait a minute, and call `get_user_state`. It should report the selection.
5. Hide the tab with nobody else on the board and call `apply_ops`. Then call `get_page_info`, which reads the room: it should list the new shapes.
6. With two tabs open, check the batch lands once, in the tab you last used.
7. Close the tab and check each tool answers with the board's URL.
8. As a view-only user, check `apply_ops` says so, with and without a tab open.

- [ ] Unit tests
- [ ] End to end tests

### Release notes

- Let agents edit tldraw.com boards through the MCP server, in the user's open tab
- Require the board to be open in a browser tab for the MCP server's clustering and screenshot tools
- Send changes made in a hidden tab, such as by an agent, instead of holding them until the tab is shown

### API changes

- Add `options.maxFrameWaitMs` to the `FpsScheduler` constructor, which runs queued work after that long when no animation frame arrives

### Code changes

| Section | LOC change |
| --- | --- |
| Core code | +1070 / -62 |
| Tests | +1601 / -2006 |
| Automated files | +3 / -1 |
| Apps | +4235 / -1711 |
| Templates | +6 / -6 |
| Config/tooling | +216 / -271 |

issue.title: feat(mcp): add page and region screenshots, and shape ids on cluster screenshots

labels.name: repo-3bfec0a7
labels.description: New feature

issue.body:
In order to let agents read a board the way a person does, zooming in on a region to read small text and starting from a view of the whole page, this PR adds a page screenshot tool with optional bounds and lets `get_cluster_screenshot` take shape ids. In 81 logged `get_cluster_screenshot` calls, agents had no way to zoom into a region. A first look at a 625-cluster page meant listing every cluster. `page` was also required on that one tool, while every other tool defaults it to 0.

```
get_page_screenshot(boardId, page = 0, bounds?: { x, y, w, h }, theme?)
  → { pageName, bounds, pageBounds? } + 1200x630 PNG, everything in view drawn
get_cluster_screenshot(boardId, page = 0, clusterIds | shapeIds, theme?)
  → page name + 1200x630 PNG of only those clusters or shapes
```

### Two tools, split on what is drawn

`get_cluster_screenshot` still draws only what it is given (now cluster ids or up to 100 shape ids), with the camera fitted to them. `get_page_screenshot` draws everything in view, either the whole page or the `bounds` rectangle. I kept the split at "only these shapes" vs "this region as it looks", not one general tool with three targeting modes, because that split is the choice a model actually has to make. Each call names exactly one target. An argument that belongs to the other tool (`bounds` on the cluster tool, `clusterIds`/`shapeIds` on the page tool) gets a clear error that names the right tool, and is never silently ignored. Null or `[]` for the unused field counts as absent.

### Reporting what the image covers

The page tool sets the render page's camera itself, using the explicit `x`/`y`/`z` viewport path that the client render page already supported but nothing sent. It doesn't ask for a content fit, so the worker knows the exact page-space rectangle in the image and returns it as `bounds`. A whole-page shot also returns `pageBounds`, the extent of the page's shapes. A model can map pixels to canvas coordinates and pick `bounds` for a closer look. The client code is unchanged; only its comment moved.

The zoom stays inside the editor's default zoom steps (5% to 800%). Outside them, `setCamera` on the render page clamps around the editor's current camera, and the image would show somewhere other than the reported rectangle. So `bounds` larger than 24000×12600 (1200×630 at 5%) is refused. A page larger than that is cropped to its centre, and the result shows this as `bounds` smaller than `pageBounds`. The page job puts no shape ids in the render token, so the URL stays the same size however big the page is.

### Spend, caching and limits

- A whole page frames on its content extent, which only a measure knows. The cluster index now stores that extent (one box per page, `CLUSTER_INDEX_FORMAT_VERSION` 1 → 2, so existing rows re-measure once). After `get_page_info`, a page shot costs one capture. Cold, it costs a measure and a capture. An empty page skips the measure.
- `bounds` shots and `shapeIds` shots never measure.
- New PNG cache keys sit beside the shape-set ones: `page-{digest}` and `region-{digest}`. A whole-page entry stores its framing in R2 metadata, so a hit spends nothing.
- Same limiter order as the cluster tool. The per-user budget is checked before the cache, the access check gates the cache read, and the per-board and global limits apply on a miss only. Measures still count against the global limit and not the per-board one.
- New failure code on the request ledger: `shape_not_found` (already in the documented vocabulary).

The per-board limit (2 captures a minute) means a third distinct region of one board inside a minute is refused. I documented this in `config.ts` and left the binding alone.

### Change type

- [x] `feature`

### Test plan

1. Point an MCP client at a preview and call `get_page_screenshot` on a board with no page: the whole first page, with `bounds` and `pageBounds` in the text.
2. Pass a `bounds` rectangle taken from that result and check the image shows that region.
3. Call `get_cluster_screenshot` with `shapeIds` from `get_cluster_info`, and with no `page`.

- [x] Unit tests

### Release notes

- Add `get_page_screenshot` to the tldraw.com MCP server, which screenshots a whole page or zooms into a rectangle and reports the page area the image covers. `get_cluster_screenshot` also accepts shape ids, and its page now defaults to the first.

### Code changes

| Section        | LOC change |
| -------------- | ---------- |
| Core code      | +2 / -2    |
| Tests          | +440 / -22 |
| Apps           | +708 / -136 |
| Config/tooling | +5 / -6    |

![Before/after: page and region screenshots, and the bounds they report](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/806f4979-41b1-4583-a6d9-dded59f36600)

issue.title: feat(arrows): keep precise anchors fixed from their nearest corner on resize
issue.body:
NOTE this is a poc/spike to see how it feels


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df9f69ce-1f54-437c-bea6-ab024b6ecdcb



---

This PR improves precise arrow bindings so that an arrow you placed at a specific spot on a shape stays there when the shape is resized or its label grows it, instead of sliding proportionally.

### Before

A precise binding stores `normalizedAnchor`, a 0–1 fraction of the bound shape's geometry bounds, and nothing touched it when the shape changed size. Resizing a 100×100 box to 200×200 moved an arrow placed 10px from its top-left corner to 20px away. Typing into a geo shape did the same: `growY` grows the shape downward and the label width grows it rightward, so anchors stretched as you typed. Anyone who had placed arrows carefully had to drag them back after every resize.

### After

When a shape with precise bindings changes size, `ArrowBindingUtil.onAfterChangeToShape` rewrites each anchor so that on each axis it keeps its distance from the nearer edge, which is the same as staying fixed relative to the nearest corner. This covers interactive resizes, label growth and programmatic `updateShape` calls.

- Anchors in the middle of an axis (within 0.01 of 0.5, such as edge-midpoint and center snaps) stay in the middle.
- If the shape shrinks past an anchor, the anchor stops at the middle of that axis rather than crossing to the far edge.
- Scale changes (`scale`, `scaleX`, `scaleY`) and open geometry (draw, line) stay proportional, because those shapes scale their contents or points along with the bounds.
- On non-rectangular outlines, the new anchor goes through the existing `updateBindingAnchorIfOutsideShape` re-snap from #9281, so it can't float off an ellipse or triangle.

- It also holds when the arrow is resized along with the shape. `ArrowShapeUtil.onResize` used to write the drag-start anchors back on every frame, which undid the adjustment. It now mirrors the current anchors only on the frame a flip toggles, so flipping a selection still mirrors arrows.
- Auto-sized text shapes are covered too. `TextShapeUtil.getMinDimensions` read an id-keyed size cache even when given an older record, so the hook saw no size change as text grew. It now measures non-current records fresh.

The behavior is controlled by a new `ArrowShapeOptions.preciseAnchorResizeBehavior: 'nearest-corner' | 'proportional'` option, which defaults to `'nearest-corner'`.

### Implementation notes

The adjustment is relative to the shape's previous state, so unlike the other arrow binding side effects it can't safely run twice. Store side effects also run on clients that receive a remote change, and that change already carries the sender's binding update. To avoid adjusting twice, `BindingOnShapeChangeOptions` now carries the change `source`, and the hook skips `'remote'` changes. Undo and redo are skipped through `isReplayingHistory()`.

This PR adds `source` to a public type. The other place to get it, `isMergingRemoteChanges`, is private on the store, and side-effect handlers already receive `source`, so threading it through seemed the least surprising option. I only added it to the shape-change hooks that need it.

Known limitations, which follow from doing this per change instead of changing what the binding stores:

- **Lossy within a gesture.** Each frame works from the previous frame, not the start of the drag. Shrinking a box past an anchor and growing it back in one drag leaves the anchor in the middle. Flipping a shape by dragging through zero width also parks its anchors in the middle.
- **Diffs replayed as `'user'`.** A diff applied with `store.applyDiff` outside `mergeRemoteChanges` gets adjusted again. The agent template's accept/reject and revert do this.
- **Concurrent resizes.** Two clients resizing the same shape at once each adjust from their own starting state, and the last binding write wins.

The way to remove all three would be to store the anchor as an edge plus an offset and resolve it in `getArrowTerminalInArrowSpace` and `getElbowTarget`. That means a binding migration, so this PR first tests whether "nearest corner" feels right.

Open question: should `'nearest-corner'` be the default for SDK users, or should we enable it only in tldraw.com to begin with?

### Change type

- [x] `improvement`

### Test plan

1. Draw a rectangle and bind a few arrows to it precisely (hold on the shape until the precise indicator appears), placing some near corners and one at an edge midpoint.
2. Resize the rectangle from different handles. Corner-adjacent arrows stay the same distance from their corner, and the midpoint arrow stays on the midpoint.
3. Type a multi-line label into the rectangle. Arrows near the top and left don't move.
4. Select a rectangle together with an arrow bound precisely to it, and resize the selection. The anchor stays fixed relative to its corner. Flip the selection, and the anchor mirrors.
5. Bind a precise arrow near the top-left of an auto-sized text shape, then type more words and lines. The arrow doesn't move.
6. Bind a precise arrow to a draw stroke and resize the stroke. The arrow stays on the stroke.

- [x] Unit tests (7 of the new tests fail when the option is set back to `'proportional'`, and the selection and text tests fail without the `onResize` and `getMinDimensions` changes)

### Release notes

- Keep precise arrows fixed relative to the nearest corner when the shape they point to is resized or grows to fit its label.

### API changes

- Added `ArrowShapeOptions.preciseAnchorResizeBehavior` (`'nearest-corner' | 'proportional'`, default `'nearest-corner'`)
- Added `source` to `BindingOnShapeChangeOptions`, passed to `onAfterChangeFromShape` and `onAfterChangeToShape`

### Code changes

| Section         | LOC change |
| --------------- | ---------- |
| Core code       | +138 / -73 |
| Tests           | +189 / -22 |
| Automated files | +4 / -1    |

labels.name: repo-3bfec0a7

issue.body:
This PR improves get_page_info's clusters: arrows join the shapes they connect, every cluster says where it sits, and labels lead with a cluster's title. Builds on #11225 and #11228.

### Before

- Arrows never joined clusters, so every arrow was its own cluster: a flowchart on staging came back as 55 clusters, 33 of them single shapes.
- Clusters had no position, so finding what was near what meant opening each one.
- Labels were keywords only: a write-up titled "#10949 · Make new images fit the view" was labelled "image · native size".

### After

- A bound arrow joins the clusters of the shapes it's bound to, at any distance. A free arrow's ends count as points, so it joins what they sit near without its box chaining unrelated shapes.
- get_page_info gives each cluster, and the page, `bounds` `{ x, y, w, h }`, or `null` when nothing was measured. The cluster index stores one box per cluster, so cached and fresh answers match.
- A label is the frame name, else the largest top-left text plus one distinguishing keyword, else what the cluster holds ("12 freehand strokes").

The get_page_info description and server instructions are rewritten to match. Cluster index format goes to 3, server to 3.7.0.

### Change type

- [x] `improvement`

### Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: arrow and binding clustering, title-led labels, page and cluster bounds (including unmeasured), and cached vs fresh get_page_info.

### Code changes

| Section   | LOC change |
| --------- | ---------- |
| Core code | +218 / -54 |
| Tests     | +427 / -15 |
| Apps      | +115 / -67 |

![Before/after: arrows join clusters, cluster bounds, and title-led labels](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22854345-b80c-4c5c-8830-c91a613e1f7b)

comment.body:
### Effect on real staging boards

I replayed 22 staging boards (28 pages) through main's clustering and this branch. Each board was measured in a real editor for page bounds, `getText` and arrow ends.

| Board | Clusters | Lone-arrow clusters | Largest cluster (shapes) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reading-path flowchart | 55 → 2 | 48 → 0 | 26 → 66 |
| Codex review | 3 → 1 | 2 → 0 | 23 → 25 |
| Attribution demo | 25 → 8 | 19 → 0 | 56 → 72 |
| QA smoke test (large), 2,159 shapes | 625 → 436 | 186 → 0 | 81 → 86 |
| Meeting board | 92 → 47 | 35 → 0 | 201 → 201 |
| Fairy retro | 205 → 188 | 15 → 0 | 485 → 408 |
| Testing playground | 96 → 87 | 27 → 14 | 543 → 531 |

- **Arrows:** lone-arrow clusters go to zero everywhere except free arrows that sit far from anything. The flowchart now splits into exactly its two charts, titled "THE STORYGRAPH TBR PICKER" and "AFTER THE FIRE".
- **Cluster size:** arrows didn't produce runaway clusters. The clusters over 100 shapes were already that size on main; they're tightly packed drawings, not arrow chains.
- **Unlabelled clusters:** these drop sharply, for example 374 → 187 on the large QA board and 33 → 0 on the flowchart.

The replay also showed the largest-text title sometimes picking decoration: "🍀", "-------", or a bookmark's URL. 0539de9909 skips titles with fewer than three letters, URLs, bookmarks and embeds, and takes the next-largest text instead. issue.title: feat(templates): take agent starter kit actions through tool calls

labels.name: repo-3bfec0a7
labels.description: ⚙️ Changes that don't affect SDK users, e.g. internal or .com changes

issue.body:
In order to make the agent starter kit's replies reliable, this PR has the model take each action through a tool call instead of writing one JSON object as text. The fairies demo showed that tool calls are the paved path: every provider supports them natively, streams them and trains its models on them, and the models give better results. This PR uses the same loop as fairies (tldraw/tldraw-internal#2707).

Read the [tour](https://teamldraw.com/api/files/pr-tour-tldraw-11147.html/view) for more detail.

### Why tool calls (from fairies)
- **JSON text broke.** Fairies had stalls, empty replies and failed parses through OpenRouter, and Sonnet sometimes wrote `<invoke>` XML instead of JSON. With tool calls, 20 local runs over Haiku, Sonnet, Gemini and GPT had no failures, and the preview had no failed replies (tldraw/tldraw-internal#2571).
- **Structured output is no alternative.** Anthropic rejects the full action schema ("The compiled grammar is too large"), and a forced JSON tool does not work with thinking on (tldraw/tldraw-internal#2705).
- **Real results let the model fix its work.** With a count result of 3, Claude, Gemini and GPT each drew 3 circles (tldraw/tldraw-internal#2707).

### Ships
- **Tool calls:** each action the agent's current mode allows is a tool, named after its `_type`, with the action's schema as its parameters. Plain text from the model is a `message` action. The JSON response schema, the assistant prefill and `supportsPrefill` are gone.
- **Streaming:** the worker reads `fullStream`. A tool call's input streams to the client as a partial action while the model writes it, so drawing still happens live. The model's reasoning streams as a `think` action: Anthropic thinking, Gemini thought summaries (`includeThoughts`) and OpenAI reasoning summaries (`reasoningSummary: 'auto'`).
- **Tool results from the browser:** the tools have no `execute`. The worker makes one model step per request and ends the stream with the number of tool calls. The browser applies each action and records its result in the chat history, then sends a follow-up request if the model called any tools. The model reads the results there.
- **Action results:** `AgentActionUtil.getResult(action, diff)` says what an action did. By default it lists the shapes it created, updated or deleted. `count-shapes` returns the count. An action util throws `ActionFailedError` for a model mistake, such as an update to a shape that does not exist: the message becomes the tool result, with no error toast.
- **Turn limit:** a turn makes at most 20 follow-up requests. Three requests before the limit, the model gets a warning to finish.
- **History:** past actions go back to the model as tool calls with their real results. Consecutive actions share one assistant turn and one results message. A history of one call per turn taught Gemini to make one call per response. An Anthropic cache marker on the last history message lets each follow-up read the history from the cache.
- **Empty replies:** an empty reply to a user's prompt is an error, with its own message when the provider's safety filter declined. An empty reply to a follow-up ends the turn.
- **Invalid tool calls:** when a call's input fails schema validation, the client does not apply it. It records the call with the validation error as its result, and the model reads the error in the next step. A call to an action that the mode does not have is dropped.
- **Failures:** when the stream ends or fails on a half-finished action, the client reverts its canvas changes and removes it from the chat history.
- **Streaming geo shapes:** a cut-off `textAlign`, such as `"midd"`, falls back to `middle`. Before, the store rejected it and the app crashed. This also happened before this PR, with JSON output.
- **Timing:** each action is timed from the end of the one before, so the times in the chat add up to the turn.

### Impacts
- **People who build on the starter kit:** action schemas reach the model as tool parameters. `buildSystemPrompt` no longer takes `withSchema`, and `shared/schema/buildResponseSchema.ts` is removed. The README and the starter kit docs describe `getResult`, `ActionFailedError` and the turn limit.
- **Cost:** a turn can make up to 20 follow-up requests. The cache marker keeps the history cheap on Claude. The kit has no per-user limit; the README says to add one before a deploy.

### Verification
- Tested locally through OpenRouter with #11103 stacked on top. Prompt: draw a farm with a barn, a fence and two animals, label everything, count the shapes, then review the drawing and fix overlaps.
  - Claude Sonnet 5: 2 of 2 turns ended with a message, after 4 follow-ups each. No errors.
  - Claude Haiku 4.5: 2 of 2 turns ended with a message, after 6 and 11 follow-ups. No errors.
- The agent template typechecks and lints.

### Known gaps
- Gemini was not tested, because it needs a Google key.
- GPT-5.6 Luna now uses its default reasoning effort. At `max` it spent almost all of its 8,192 output tokens on reasoning and drew nothing. It was not tested again after this change.

### Decisions
- Invalid tool calls are fixed the same way in fairies: tldraw/tldraw-internal#2793.
- No OpenRouter code here. #11103 adds optional gateway base URLs on top.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

comment.body: hey reading through this I have some directional questions, mainly with regard to switching from the action schema to tool calls. it feels a little awkward, namely it feels like we're only partially opting into tool calls in a way that doesn't really give us much new stuff, but adds a bit confusion because we have to opt out of certain other parts of tool calls. for example, tool calls assume tools will be executed on the server, but currently we execute our actions on the client. because of this, we have all tools return a dummy result from the server (the `'Done. Any data this action gathers comes in your next request.'` bit in `AgentService.ts`), and if it errors on the client we have our own way of reporting it. also, we also have a _different_ dummy way of representing the tool response in the history (the `output: { type: 'text', value: 'ok' },` bit in `buildMessages.ts`, which is also kind of confusing so my question I guess is what specifically are we getting form using tool calls aside from there was that strange bug that this fixed? because I think from the standpoint of code clarity this makes it a bit more difficult to reason about assuming we address this, I have some other smaller nits: 1. it seems like we lose intratool streaming? not sure exactly where this is coming from but from trying out this branch, tools themselves don't seem to be streamed in anymore. this isn't a must have but it's really nice in decreasing perceived latency for end users, and it looks really nice 2. the tool response seen by the model 3. this is less of an issue, but now we send native reasoning back as the bespoke "think" action, which might confuse models when they see it in their history. probably fine though? 4. in `ReviewActionUtil.ts` we still reference the old `'[ACTION]: '` way of putting tool results in history, we should reword this 5. also seeing some old bad behavior surface (pics attached) where an agent schedules a review and thinks its done the review so it responds as if it has, but then it gets autoprompted by the scheduled review to do it again, resulting in the 2 kind of repetitive messages from the model. this is one of those tricky things that pops up from time to time.

issue.body:
This PR improves `T.linkUrl` so that shapes can link into desktop apps: a bookmark on a board can open a specific Codex thread (`codex://threads/<id>`), a VS Code file (`vscode://file/…`), or a Slack channel (`slack://…`).

### Before

`linkUrl` accepted only `http:`, `https:` and `mailto:`. Bookmark, geo, note, image and video shapes validate their `url` prop with it, so a shape with an app link failed validation. That happened locally and on the sync server alike. The only workaround was hosting an https page that redirects to the app link.

### After

`linkUrl` also accepts app links into a fixed allow list of desktop apps: `claude:`, `codex:`, `cursor:`, `discord:`, `figma:`, `jetbrains:`, `linear:`, `notion:`, `obsidian:`, `slack:`, `spotify:`, `vscode:`, `windsurf:` and `zed:`. Every other scheme is still rejected, including `javascript:`, `data:`, `file:` and `localhost:3000`. The link dialog relies on that last one being rejected so it can prefix `https://`.

Bookmarks with a non-http(s) url skip unfurling and stay url-only bookmarks. A bookmark asset's `src` is a `T.srcUrl`, which rejects app links (and `mailto:`), so the fetched asset would fail validation. On tldraw.com the unfurl endpoint also accepts only http(s).

SPEC.md in `@tldraw/validate` gets a new UR7 and a pointer from UR1. Every shape whose `url` uses `linkUrl` (bookmark, geo, image, note, video) gets a migration so older SDKs keep working (see below).

### Implementation notes

- **Named app links, not deep links.** "Deep link" already means the SDK's `?d=` links to shapes, pages and viewports (`TLDeepLink`, `editor.navigateToDeepLink`), so these are called app links throughout.
- **An allow list, not "any scheme but these".** New schemes are rejected until someone adds them, so a scheme that runs script or reaches local content can't slip through. The cost is that the list needs updating as people ask for apps. Browsers still show their own "Open <app>?" prompt before handing off to an external handler.
- **Apps whose links usually circulate as https are left out.** Teams and Zoom share `https://teams.microsoft.com/…` and `https://zoom.us/j/…` links, which already validate and offer to open the app.
- **Older SDKs get a blank link instead of an error.** Each of the five shapes gets an `AllowAppLinkUrls` props migration. Its `up` is a no-op, because every stored url is still valid. Its `down` blanks any url the old `linkUrl` would reject. On a shared board, a client on an older SDK then sees the shape with an empty link instead of failing to validate the record.

### Change type

- [x] `improvement`

### Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: UR7 covers allow-listed app links (with and without `//`, mixed case), and rejects `localhost:3000`, an unlisted app scheme, and unsafe schemes in `javascript://` form and in mixed case
- [x] Migration tests: each shape's `down` blanks a app link and keeps `''`, http(s), mailto and relative urls; `up` leaves them alone
- [x] Bookmark tests: creating a bookmark from a app link, and changing a bookmark's url to one, don't fetch metadata

### Release notes

- Allow app links into apps such as VS Code, Cursor, Slack and Figma in shape links and bookmarks.

### Code changes

| Section   | LOC change |
| --------- | ---------- |
| Core code | +110 / -2  |
| Tests     | +73 / -0   |
| Docs      | +2 / -1    |
| Assets    | +5 / -5    |

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
